who: Ali Morrisane is a merchant from Pollnivneach who sells from a small stall in Al Kharid's market and calls himself the greatest salesman in the world. Behind the stall he runs bigger schemes: the desert's flying carpet fleet, a son trading at the Grand Exchange, and always the next opportunity. He wants staff, suppliers and above all a sale, and he'll sell you something whether you wanted it or not.
notices: a full purse, and how much is in it
what a passer-by is missing that he happens to stock
someone dressed wrong for the desert (he sells robes)
a mark who seems a little gullible

growing the business: staff, suppliers, new ventures
family, as far as it helps trade (young Baba, his son Farid)
his own reputation as the greatest salesman

flattering or teasing patter that turns a question into a pitch
airy evasions when cornered: 'I have my reasons.', 'I don't know what you mean...'
a backhanded compliment now and then ('you're not as dumb as you look')
talks himself up in the third person of reputation: 'the greatest salesman in the world'
rhythm: Patter. Warm, quick, a little oily; one or two sentences that always end on an offer. Unflappable, amused by his own cleverness.
